post.description:
External callers (Node-RED, scripts, third-party apps) post here with `type` and `context` (vars used by the template). The service handles routing, throttling, and channel dispatch. Caller does NOT need to know channels, credentials, or templates.

With `idempotency_key` the fire belongs to an **episode**: the first `status: firing` opens it (an incident) and notifies, repeats while it is open notify nothing, `status: resolved` closes it and sends `resolved_type` if one was given. `episode` in the response says what happened. `test: true` ignores the key.

`test: true` marks the notification as a test. Only an `admin` caller's test also skips throttle, quiet hours and de-duplication; a `fire` key's test is gated like any other fire — `suppressed_reason` says why one was held.

get.description: Returns the overall service status; a caller with `read` (API key or signed-in user) also gets the version and the per-component map. Always returns HTTP 200 — inspect the body to determine status. For a pass/fail probe that fails on essential-component outages, use ``/v1/health/ready`` (returns 503 when not ready).

Returns HTTP 200 when every essential component (database, rule engine, delivery worker) is up, and HTTP 503 when one is down — so an orchestrator or the container healthcheck acts on a dead engine or retry worker instead of a body that always says 200 (F32). The body is shaped like `/v1/health`'s for the same caller.
